requirement:
For backends that accept explicit cache checkpoints, when the backend and model
support prompt caching, every provider request MUST place one cache checkpoint
after the system prompt of {cite}`requirements.authoring.prompt_parts` and
another at the end of its last message, so each request reuses the tool
definitions and system prompt that earlier assessments of its kind sent, and
the conversation its own earlier requests sent. Cache checkpoints MUST NOT
change the content of a request.

For OpenAI, which caches matching prompt prefixes automatically, the harness
MUST keep the system prompt and tool definitions unchanged across requests in
one conversation and replay prior conversation content in its original order.
It MUST NOT insert checkpoint blocks.
rationale:
The tests cover every obligation in `requirements.authoring.cache_checkpoints`. I found no unacknowledged gap.

**Explicit-checkpoint backend (Bedrock).** `RigProvider::complete` calls `place_cache_checkpoints` only when `self.caches` is set. Bedrock is the only backend that sets it, so no other explicit-checkpoint backend goes untested.
- **One checkpoint after the system prompt and one at the end of the last message, on every request.** `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[claude_requests_carry_cache_checkpoints_and_record_cache_usage]` runs a Claude model and checks both requests, the second of which follows a reasoning turn and a tool result. For each body it asserts these things:
  - `system` has two entries, and the second is the `cachePoint` block.
  - The last block of the last message is the `cachePoint` block.
  - `cachePoint` occurs exactly twice in the body.
- **"When the backend and model support caching".** `bedrock_caches` is unit-tested in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/providers.rs#mod[tests]/fn[cache_checkpoints_are_requested_for_caching_models]`. It accepts Claude, Claude through an ARN, and Nova. It rejects Llama and the fixture model. The CLI test also checks that a non-caching model's request contains no `cachePoint`.
- **Checkpoints must not change content.** There are two checks:
  - The CLI test compares each cached body, with `without_cache_points` applied, to the matching body from the uncached model. The two must be equal.
  - The unit test asserts that `place_cache_checkpoints` changes only `options.cache`. It does this by comparing the serialized request to an expected request that differs only in that option, and it repeats the check after a reasoning turn.
- **Reuse of the system prompt across assessments of a kind.** This follows from `requirements.authoring.prompt_parts`, which the requirement cites as context. It is not reassessed here.

**OpenAI.** `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[openai_responses_replays_tool_calls_and_records_usage]` checks these things across both requests:
- `instructions` is non-empty and identical across the two requests.
- `tools` is identical across the two requests.
- The second request's `input` starts with exactly the first request's `input`, followed by the replayed `function_call` and `function_call_output` in order.
- `assert_no_checkpoints` walks the whole body and rejects any `cachePoint` or `cache_control` key. It also rejects `cache_point` or `cache_checkpoint` as a `type` value. This enforces "MUST NOT insert checkpoint blocks".

Both the Bedrock and OpenAI tests carry `{test}` references to this requirement.

text: :::{req} cache_checkpoints
For backends that accept explicit cache checkpoints, when the backend and model
support prompt caching, every provider request MUST place one cache checkpoint
after the system prompt of {cite}`requirements.authoring.prompt_parts` and
another at the end of its last message, so each request reuses the tool
definitions and system prompt that earlier assessments of its kind sent, and
the conversation its own earlier requests sent. Cache checkpoints MUST NOT
change the content of a request.
For OpenAI, which caches matching prompt prefixes automatically, the harness
MUST keep the system prompt and tool definitions unchanged across requests in
one conversation and replay prior conversation content in its original order.
It MUST NOT insert checkpoint blocks.
:::{req} prompt_parts
Each assessment conversation MUST send its prompt as a system prompt followed by
one user message, the subject message, filled from the first and second text
blocks of the prompt requirement for the assessment's kind. The kinds are
test-adequacy requirement, structural requirement, example, citation review, site
review, and a verifier of each of those. A system prompt MUST be the same for
every assessment of its kind, so every placeholder whose value depends on the
subject MUST be in the subject message.
